listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Sunday, October 25. Our lead story is from the UFC. Alexander Volkanovski defended his featherweight title for the second time this year on Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. He knocked out undefeated challenger Movsar Evloev at four minutes and fifty-four seconds of the second round. Petr Yan also kept his title on the same card. He beat Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision in the co-main event and completed their trilogy. Now to the front page. In the NBA, Kevin Durant scored twenty-two points and Reed Sheppard hit five three-pointers. The Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks one twenty-one to one fourteen in Atlanta's home opener. The 49ers play the Falcons today. San Francisco activated receiver Christian Kirk from injured reserve and released lineman Kevin Givens. In world news, Elon Musk says SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection. He accuses Ukraine of using the network for military activity in violation of its terms. Service has been restored. And The Lever has an investigation into how AIPAC is routing millions of dollars through groups promoting women, reproductive rights and Latino candidates. It says AI interests are adopting the same strategy. Now the sections. In tech, Anthropic launched Claude Models on Google Cloud, with Google Cloud access controls and marketplace billing. In politics, NPR reports a rise of economic populism in both parties as the midterms approach. In world news, large protests took place across Europe on Saturday, and almost one thousand people were arrested after clashes in France. Brazilian voters choose between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. In sports, Petr Yan's win at UFC 333 and a preview of the matchup between Fred Warner and Bijan Robinson are worth a look. In Atlanta, Urbanize shows aerial photos of the city's newest baseball venue taking shape. In architecture, Qonic is moving toward letting users author complete BIM models from scratch. In science, NASA ran a five hundred second hot fire test of an RS-25 engine at Stennis Space Center. That is the brief. Have a good day. This is the Sunday edition. Here is the week in review. Anthropic prepares IPO, France imposes curfews, 49ers reach 6-0. Anthropic led the AI news. Before an expected IPO, it told investors that quarterly revenue rose nearly 50% to $16.8bn (w2). It also committed shares to a new Public Benefit Fund, which BBC put at 5% (w1, w123). Other releases: Claude Models on Google Cloud (w99), API version 2026-10-21 with new SDKs (w77), Claude working in Google Docs, Sheets and Slides (w74), and Agent Skills donated to the Agentic AI Foundation (w95). The Lever reported critically on draft AI legislation circulated by Anthropic (w24). In BIM, Revizto shipped an MCP server with Claude skills (w96). Flaws in PHP that AI found set off a global security response (w72). France imposed nightly curfews after rioting, and almost 1,000 people were arrested (w58, w150). Protests also spread to Milan, Rome, Madrid and Lisbon (w149). A source told NPR that the U.S. and Israel are planning for a possible attack on Iran in early November (w94), and Houthi attacks led the U.S. to pull some diplomats from Saudi Arabia (w75). Alberta voted to stay in Canada (w25), and Ebola cases were confirmed in Nigeria and Kenya (w52, w107). In the U.S., courts and county officials disputed federal efforts to find noncitizen voters (w51, w97). In Atlanta, the council voted 8-7 to sell the detention center to Fulton County for $68 million (w28), and the debate over Beltline rail went on (w17, w131). In sports, the 49ers went 6-0 ahead of their game in Atlanta (w27). The Rockets won all three games of opening week (w73, w121, w141). At UFC 333, Volkanovski and Yan both kept their titles (w140, w152).

lead.title: Alexander Volkanovski stops Movsar Evloev in 2nd round to retain title
lead.note: Alexander Volkanovski defended his featherweight title for the second time this year on Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. He knocked out undefeated challenger Movsar Evloev at 4:54 of the second round. ESPN described the win as dominant. Evloev had entered the fight without a loss, so the finish carries extra weight. Volkanovski has now successfully held the belt twice in 2026. Earlier on the card, Petr Yan also kept his title, beating Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision in the co-main event. That fight completed their trilogy, and Yan won the last two meetings. For a reader who follows the UFC, this is the main result of the weekend, and it keeps both champions on top of their divisions.
